summary: Milestone 2026.05.258 recorded 0 experiments in the timing window — the thirty-third consecutive empty-timing-window retro. Both RTX 3090 GPUs were idle at 0% utilization (41C/49C); no compute-bound tasks appeared in timing scope, so gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks remains null. The timing-script look-back window not being anchored to the conductor-state.json activation timestamp continues as the confirmed root cause of the zero-experiment streak.
bottlenecks_identified: Timing-script look-back window not anchored to conductor-state.json activation timestamp — root cause of 33 consecutive empty-window retros; retro fires before committed experiment artifacts fall inside the look-back range.

No post-activation dispatch verification gate — retro executes immediately after milestone activation with no minimum-experiment-count sentinel, allowing empty retros to be filed while real work is still in flight.
Paper v6 toolchain missing — blocked any theory-update experiments that depend on a local LaTeX/paper source tree (consistent with capstone v258 findings).
KV260 SD card absent — hardware continuity task escalated to operator for fourth consecutive milestone; no programmatic resolution path available to the conductor.
improvements_suggested: Fix timing-script look-back to use conductor-state.json 'activated_at' timestamp as the floor instead of a fixed trailing window; this single fix resolves the 33-milestone empty-window streak structurally.
Wire a zero-artifact alarm: if no experiment artifact lands within 60 minutes of milestone activation, emit a WARNING commit and halt retro until at least one non-retro experiment completes.
Require a milestone-open sentinel commit at activation time so the timing script always has at least one in-scope commit as an anchor.
Add paper v6 LaTeX toolchain precondition check to the milestone activation manifest — block paper-theory tasks from queuing until pdflatex + source tree presence is verified.
Escalate KV260 SD card as operator-action-required in known-issues.md with a hard milestone skip-limit (e.g., skip no more than 2 milestones before declaring the KV260 track suspended).
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Fix timing-script look-back to conductor-state.json 'activated_at' timestamp — resolves the 33-milestone empty-window retro streak in one edit with no experiment changes required.

Wire zero-artifact alarm at 60 minutes post-activation — prevents future milestones from filing empty retros while real work is still running, giving the operator an actionable signal instead of a silent empty report.

Activate the first non-retro experiment in the same conductor session as milestone activation — breaks the stall pattern by ensuring at least one compute or synthesis task completes before the retro executes.
meta_reflection: This is the thirty-third consecutive milestone where the timing window returned zero experiments — an unambiguous systemic failure in the retro's data-collection layer, not in experiment execution itself. The recurring bottleneck (timing-script look-back not anchored to activation timestamp) has been identified and documented in at least the prior six retros; the leverage action is surgical (one-line change to scripts/session-metrics.py or equivalent), yet it has not been applied. Operationally, the milestone appears to have executed real work (capstone synthesis, cascade fix, Phase 1 ship prep) that the timing script simply cannot see; until the look-back anchor is fixed, retros will continue to under-report and any efficiency analysis derived from them will be structurally unreliable.
